question: Q9 Consumer-boycott survey 2025: perceived beneficiaries of the boycott
indicator: Share agreeing/strongly agreeing that some party benefits from the Israel-affiliated product boycott (PKAEN survey)
unit: % of respondents who "setuju atau sangat setuju" (combined agree + strongly agree)
ref_period_and_type: Survey published 2025-05-15 (fieldwork dates not stated in the article)
scope_base: n=810; cities described as highly sensitive to the boycott issue (Yogyakarta, Lombok, Pekanbaru, Aceh, Bandung); with PS2PM Yogyakarta; method not stated
geography: P: five Indonesian cities selected for high boycott sensitivity (Yogyakarta, Lombok, Pekanbaru, Aceh, Bandung); not Jakarta, not national
quote: [P2-TFS-S16] Sebesar 73,1 persen masyarakat setuju atau sangat setuju bahwa ada pihak yang diuntungkan oleh boikot || [P2-TFS-S16] melibatkan 810 responden || [P2-TFS-S16] Kamis, 15 Mei 2025, 20:33 WIB
commentary_by_source_or_analysis: Source commentary: the survey director argues the boycott may serve business competition and risks layoffs. Analysis: this measures perceived beneficiaries, not own boycott participation or intent; selection of high-sensitivity cities and an unfamiliar institute argue for low weight; single outlet (RMOL).
confidence: low (single outlet, unfamiliar institute, selected cities, advocacy framing, no method or fieldwork dates)
gaps: Questionnaire, fieldwork dates and the institute track record not seen; no Jakarta cut.
notes: Not a measure of boycott prevalence.

question: Q9 Consumer-boycott survey 2025: approval of the boycott (Median)
indicator: Approval of boycott of Israel-affiliated products (Median online survey)
reported_fact_value: 80.2 agree in total (50.5 strongly agree + 29.7 agree); 12.8 disagree
unit: % of respondents (strongly agree and agree are additive)
scope_base: publisher: Media Survei Nasional (Median); n=643; online Google Form distributed through Meta social media; respondents from all provinces; convenience sample
quote: [P2-TFS-S17] 80,2% responden setuju atas aksi boikot terhadap produk-produk terafiliasi Israel, dengan rincian 50,5% sangat setuju dan 29,7% merasa setuju. Sisanya sebanyak 12,8% mengaku tidak setuju. || [P2-TFS-S17] survei ini dilakukan secara daring berbasis Google Form melalui media sosial Meta pada 8-13 September 2025. Sebanyak 643 responden terlibat, berasal dari seluruh provinsi di Indonesia. || [P2-TFS-S17] 5 Oktober 2025 pukul 09.30 WIB
commentary_by_source_or_analysis: Source commentary: reasons listed include economic sanction (20.9%) and humanitarian solidarity (18.8%); among 12.8% disagreeing, 29.3% feared domestic economic harm. Analysis: approval of boycott is not the same as own purchase behaviour, and a self-selected social-media sample is not representative; Median original page (median.or.id) returned 404 so the figure rests on the GoodStats relay.
confidence: low (self-selected social-media sample, n=643, relay only)
gaps: Median original not opened; no age or Jakarta cut; no behavioural measure.
notes: Reported-agreement figure only; S-05 (89%) is a stated preference to replace boycotted products with local Islamic brands; its base is not stated and it is not a boycott-participation measure. Derived, not in the source: 100 - 80.2 - 12.8 = 7.0; note that GoodStats words 12.8% as "Sisanya" although 80.2 + 12.8 = 93.0. Run 3 verification (V3-B, 2026-10-17): remainder removed from the unit cell.

quote: [P2-TFS-S18] 89 persen responden lebih memilih mengganti produk global yang diboikot dengan brand lokal Islami. || [P2-TFS-S18] Kamis, 06 Maret 2025
commentary_by_source_or_analysis: Source commentary (Yuswohady, Inventure): the change is a shift in consumption patterns; local Islamic brands have an opportunity. Analysis: undefined base; a marketing-research claim from a consultancy conference.

notes: Run 3 verification (V3-B, 2026-10-17): the 89% is a stated preference to substitute boycotted global products with local Islamic brands, not boycott participation; base not defined (the article frames "konsumen muslim"); no n, population or fieldwork date. Low weight.

question: Q9 Protest incidents in Jakarta 2025: pro-Palestine rally at the US Embassy
indicator: Mass pro-Palestine action at the US Embassy, Jakarta, with police deployment
reported_fact_value: 1,994 joint police personnel deployed for the "Aksi Bela Palestina" alliance action at the US Embassy on Jl. Medan Merdeka Selatan on 2025-01-26; the article reports no action at any restaurant or brand outlet.
unit: count of police personnel deployed (event: one rally)
scope_base: one rally; Kapolres Metro Jakarta Pusat statement
quote: [P2-TFS-S19] Gedung Kedutaan Besar (Kedubes) Amerika Serikat (AS) di Jl. Medan Merdeka Selatan, Jakarta Pusat di geruduk oleh aliansi Aksi Bela Palestina, Minggu (26/1). Sebanyak 1.994 personel gabungan pun dikerahkan || [P2-TFS-S19] Minggu, 26 Januari 2025 | 19.54 WIB
commentary_by_source_or_analysis: Analysis: the target was a government embassy and the Palestine conflict, not a Western consumer brand; the article does not mention brand boycotts. Evidence of political mobilisation level, not of brand-targeted protest.
confidence: high for the event; low relevance to brand risk
gaps: Whether any boycott slogans were used is not reported.
notes: Pre-2025 outlet-level incidents (Makassar, Samarinda, Surabaya, Nov 2023-Jun 2024) were not in Jakarta and are pre-window.

question: Q9 Investment climate: FDI/total investment realisation 2025 (Kementerian Investasi dan Hilirisasi/BKPM)
indicator: Realised investment FY2025: total, PMA (foreign) and PMDN (domestic)
reported_fact_value: Total IDR 1,931.2 trillion (+12.7% yoy; 101.3% of the IDR 1,905.6tn target); PMA IDR 900.9tn (46.6% of total, +0.1% yoy); PMDN IDR 1,030.3tn (53.4%, +26.6% yoy). 2024 comparator in the same article: total IDR 1,714.2tn, PMA IDR 900.2tn.
ref_period_and_type: full year 2025 (Jan-Dec); announced 2026-01-15; Kontan article printed 2026-01-15 14:41 WIB
scope_base: BKPM realisation statistics (sector scope exclusions not checked)
quote: [P2-TFS-S21] Kementerian Investasi dan Hilirisasi/Badan Koordinasi Penanaman Modal (BKPM) melaporkan realisasi investasi sepanjang tahun 2025 mencapai Rp 1.931,2 triliun. || [P2-TFS-S21] realisasi Penanaman Modal Asing (PMA) mencapai Rp 900,9 triliun, meningkat tipis 0,1% yoy dengan porsi 46,6% dari total realisasi. || [P2-TFS-S21] Kamis, 15 Januari 2026 / 14:41 WIB
commentary_by_source_or_analysis: Source commentary: growth slowed from 20.8% in 2024; global uncertainty cited by the minister. Analysis: PMA was flat in rupiah terms (+0.1%), so foreign-investor appetite was stable, not rising; a USD series was not read.
confidence: high (tier 3 relay of an official announcement; Metro TV carries the same numbers)
gaps: Official BKPM press release/ SPSE tables not opened; USD figure not captured.
notes: Relay of a ministerial press conference; Metro TV (printed 2026-07-15, republished) agrees on PMA 900.9 and PMDN 1,030.3. Run 3 verification (V3-B, 2026-10-17): primary source BKPM press release printed Kamis 15 Jan 2026 (REG-043) confirms total Rp1.931,2tn, +12.7%, 101.3% of target, PMA Rp900.9tn (46.6%), PMDN Rp1.030,3tn (53.4%). The PMA +0.1% and PMDN +26.6% growth rates are relay-only (Kontan).

reported_fact_value: Total IDR 1,010.6 trillion (49.5% of the IDR 2,041.3tn 2026 target; +7.2% yoy); PMA IDR 507.6tn (50.2%); PMDN IDR 502.9tn (49.8%); jobs 1,448,862.
ref_period_and_type: H1 2026 (Jan-Jun, cumulative); announced 2026-07-16 at Istana Merdeka
pub_date_printed: 2026-07-16 14.52 WIB (Katadata); 2026-07-16 16.30 WIB (DDTC); BKPM release printed Jumat 2026-07-17 (press conference 2026-07-16)
quote: [P2-TFS-S22] realisasi investasi Indonesia sepanjang semester I 2026 mencapai Rp1.010,6 triliun atau 49,5% dari target investasi tahun ini senilai Rp2.041,3 triliun. Nilai tersebut tumbuh 7,2% || [P2-TFS-S22] Penanaman Modal Asing (PMA) senilai Rp507,6 triliun atau 50,2% dari total realisasi || [P2-TFS-S23] PMDN mencapai Rp502,9 triliun atau 49,8% dan PMA-nya mencapai Rp507,6 triliun || [P2-TFS-S22] 16/7/2026, 14.52 WIB

gaps: Official BKPM release (printed Jumat 17 Jul 2026, REG-044) opened by V3-B and confirms all stored figures. No PMA growth rate is stored: the earlier +17.3% clause was removed (unopened source, derived).

question: Q9 Investment climate: H1 2026 sources of PMA and Jakarta share
indicator: Top PMA source countries (USD) and DKI Jakarta share of total realised investment, H1 2026
reported_fact_value: PMA by origin: Singapore USD 8.8bn, Hong Kong USD 7.6bn, China USD 3.9bn, Japan USD 1.9bn, United States USD 1.7bn. DKI Jakarta was the largest province with IDR 173.6tn, 17.2% of national realised investment (PMA+PMDN), ahead of West Java IDR 138.1tn. Switzerland not listed in the top five.
unit: USD billion by origin (PMA); IDR trillion and % for Jakarta (PMA+PMDN combined)
scope_base: BKPM realisation; Jakarta figure is PMA+PMDN combined, not PMA only
quote: [P2-TFS-S23] Singapura dengan realisasi investasi senilai US$8,8 miliar, Hong Kong senilai US$7,6 miliar, China senilai US$3,9 miliar, Jepang senilai US$1,9 miliar, dan Amerika Serikat (AS) senilai US$1,7 miliar. || [P2-TFS-S22] DKI Jakarta menjadi provinsi dengan realisasi investasi PMA dan PMDN terbesar selama Januari-Juni dengan Rp173,6 triliun atau 17,2% dari total investasi nasional.
commentary_by_source_or_analysis: Source commentary (minister, via DDTC): "for the first time in ten years China invests more aggressively through Hong Kong". notes: Run 3 verification (V3-B): H1 country figures and the Jakarta share are a relay of the press conference and are not in the official BKPM release (REG-044), which gives Q2 only (Hong Kong first with USD5bn; DKI Jakarta Rp94.9tn in Q2); the minister's "first time in ten years" remark concerns Q2.
